main_result.title: The public mismatch benchmark now has a separate exact analyzer that locates token divergence relative to the canonical decision-certificate boundary instead of using token mismatch as a proxy for score/sign mismatch.

artifact.inputs: canonical and fast JSONL files emitted by decision_stat_mismatch_microbenchmark.py
outputs: divergence before/at certificate versus after certificate

main_result.decision_rule: For the frozen first-match <answer>[A-D]</answer> scorer, token divergence strictly after the canonical certificate is irrelevant to the current score/sign policy if no other downstream observer consumes the suffix. Divergence at or before certificate is only diagnostic; it still must be followed by direct deterministic score/sign comparison.
main_result.why_this_matters: The vLLM #51187 trace establishes a large response-object->token gap, while the NeurIPS 2025 numerical-nondeterminism paper establishes that runtime changes can cross the final-answer/accuracy boundary. The new analyzer is the missing measurement bridge needed to quantify where an executable repeated-inference trace crosses from token difference into decision difference.

measurement_validity_rules: Never classify token divergence as harmful solely by position; compare the protected deterministic score/sign directly.
Use the certificate boundary only for a frozen prefix-monotone scorer whose suffix cannot revise the parsed decision.
Keep runtime fingerprint and canonical-instability diagnostics alongside all mismatch rates.
scope_guards: No GPU/vLLM inference was available in this run, so the analyzer has not yet consumed a live token-divergent dataset.
The analyzer does not widen the paired-sign verifier contract to stateful or interactive evaluations; those require next-state preservation too.
No forbidden semantic inputs were read.

frontier.action: Obtain or execute a public token-divergent repeated-inference dataset under a fully recorded fingerprint and run both repository analyzers to measure token->score and score-pair->sign gaps directly.
Add exact confidence bounds by fingerprint for rare score/sign mismatch, including a fail-closed rule when canonical repeats themselves are unstable.
Extend prefix certificates to deterministic JSON/schema parsers and compare canonical certificate latency with full-completion latency.

exact_next_action: Find a public raw repeated-inference artifact with actual token divergence, or run the benchmark when a compatible GPU/vLLM runtime is available; then quantify first-token divergence relative to certificate, direct score mismatch, and oriented-sign mismatch under the same fingerprint.
